## Proposed change
Resolves a bug in the Transport NSW integration (Issue #96690) where the default sensor values are `n/a` instead of `None`. As these sensor types are expecting a value of type `int` this causes the entites to break. No futher polled value updates to these entities are applied 

Additionally, I've set the StateClass and DeviceClasses on the entities

issue_context.title: Transport NSW: Invalid default value "n/a", missing device class and state classes on Entities
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Errors being logged due to the inital sensor value being set to "n/a" instead of 'None' when it shoudl be of type int. This results in entities no longer being created and syncing for hese entites never occurs.

`Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor
Source: components/sensor/__init__.py:594
Integration: Sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: July 14, 2023 at 22:01:32 (13 occurrences)
Last logged: July 14, 2023 at 22:01:46

Error adding entities for domain sensor with platform transport_nsw
Error while setting up transport_nsw platform for sensor
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/sensor/__init__.py", line 590, in state
    numerical_value = int(value)
                      ^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'n/a'

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 504, in async_add_entities
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 788, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.add_to_platform_finish()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1006, in add_to_platform_finish
    self.async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 742, in async_write_ha_state
    self._async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 810, in _async_write_ha_state
    state = self._stringify_state(available)
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 748, in _stringify_state
    if (state := self.state) is None:
                 ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/sensor/__init__.py", line 594, in state
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: Sensor sensor.nsw_bus_260_north_sydney has device class 'None', state class 'None' unit 'min' and suggested precision 'None' thus indicating it has a numeric value; however, it has the non-numeric value: 'n/a' (<class 'str'>)
`

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.7.2

ValueError: Sensor sensor.nsw_bus_260_north_sydney has device class 'None', state class 'None' unit 'min' and suggested precision 'None' thus indicating it has a numeric value; however, it has the non-numeric value: 'n/a' (<class 'str'>)

Additionally, I'll add the missing configuration via the UI once the inital bug fixes are merged

review_comments: When I check the python library, in the readme it states that if something is unavailable or has an error, it returns "n/a" as well. So this change would only fix the initialization of the sensor, but when an error occurs (or probably some other event happens) it will still return "n/a". So maybe this should be fixed in the library first before fixing it here.

Good catch, I've updated the logic to consider and handle this case. The HA integration is currently broken as it does not handle the response "n/a" from the lib inline with what HA expects. The context of why the lib responds in the way it does would be for the maintaners of that lib to determine.
